advisory.finding: `--resume` checks only schema_version, corpus, corpus_digest and match_threshold. It never compares the runner or model that produced the saved records. If the operator resumes with a different provider config, for example without `REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE` (the docs say the stores then fall back to the built-in default model), the run silently mixes Bedrock records with default-model records into one summary. That is the cross-provenance contamination this change was meant to prevent.
scenarios: An interrupted Bedrock run is resumed in a shell without the provider overlay. The early rows come from Bedrock, the later rows from the default model, and the summary aggregates both.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the resume-refusal test match the exact field token (e.g. `f"refused: {field} differs"`) rather than a substring that `corpus_digest` also satisfies
evidence: Commit message: "It now exits 2 and names the field when schema_version, corpus, corpus_digest or match_threshold differs"
advisory.finding: The resume-refusal test checks that the error names the field with a bare substring match (`field in err`). For the `corpus` case, "corpus" is a substring of "corpus_digest". If resume_mismatch or _load_resume reported the wrong field (for example, always `corpus_digest`), the test would still pass, so the contract that the error names the mismatched field is not really checked for `corpus`.
scenarios: A regression makes resume_mismatch return the wrong key, or the message print `corpus_digest` while only `corpus` differs. The parametrized `corpus` case stays green.
advisory.suggested_fix: Replace `assert field in capsys.readouterr().err` with `assert f"--resume refused: {field} differs" in capsys.readouterr().err`.

dropped.finding: The new `ran_model` provenance field is always null unless the config uses a fallback chain. The runner sets `provider_provenance["ran_model"]` only inside `if fallback_targets:`, and `provenance_for` records the resolved model under `model`, not `ran_model`. So the field the docs call 'the provider-reported ran_model' is null on every record of the committed Bedrock run. That null looks the same whether the provider reported nothing, the provenance block was missing, or the harness read the wrong key.
scenarios: Single-model Bedrock config (the documented command): every record says ran_model=null, so the served model is never attested.
dropped.suggested_fix: In `_provenance`, use `served.get("ran_model") or served.get("model")`, or record `provider_provenance.model` as its own field, so a single-model run attests its served model. Update the docs sentence to match.
